entities.summary: Lubentius was a Christian saint venerated by the Catholic Church, who served as a patron for boatmen on the River Lahn. He is believed to have been born into a family of modest means and received a classical education. Lubentius's devotion to Christianity led him to dedicate his life to spreading the faith, and he eventually became a bishop in the region. His teachings and legacy had a lasting impact on the development of Christianity in the region, and he is still revered today as a symbol of faith and devotion. Lubentius's feast day, October 13, is celebrated by Catholics around the world, and his image is often invoked by those seeking protection and guidance on their journeys. According to legend, Lubentius possessed the ability to communicate with the spirits of the dead, and he used this gift to help the living navigate the complexities of the afterlife. This extraordinary claim has been the subject of much debate and speculation, with some historians arguing that it may be a mythical or metaphorical account of Lubentius's life. Nevertheless, his legacy as a saint and a patron continues to be felt, and he remains an important figure in the history of Christianity.
